question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the September 2026 meeting?
resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

# Research report 1 of 2

I worked only from material dated on or before 2026-09-10. A few search results described later events, including the August CPI release on Sept 11 and the post-meeting decision. I left those out completely.

## 1. Resolution source
- I couldn't load the Fed's open-market page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm); the connection was refused. Secondary sources show the target range at **3.50%-3.75%**, so the starting upper bound is 3.75%.
- 2026-09-03: The effective fed funds rate was 3.63%, per FRED, quoted secondhand. [predictionmarketspicks](https://predictionmarketspicks.com/articles/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026-kalshi-polymarket-futures)
- The FOMC meets Sept 15-16, 2026, and the statement comes out Sept 16. [fedratecalc](https://fedratecalc.com/fomc-meeting-schedule/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. This cycle the debate is between a 25 bp **hike** and a hold. Markets price essentially no chance of a cut.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-04: August payrolls came in at +162k, against a consensus of about 53k. Unemployment held at 4.1% and wages were up 3.1% from a year earlier. July was revised from -23k to +21k. More than two-thirds of the gain came from leisure/hospitality and local government, largely reversing earlier drops in those sectors. CME odds of a September hike went from about 50-50 to about 60%. PNC said a hike was likely "absent a weak core CPI print." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-august-2026.html), [PNC](https://www.pnc.com/content/dam/pnc-com/pdf/aboutpnc/EconomicReports/EconomicUpdates/2026/PNC_Economics_Research_Payrolls_4_September_2026.pdf), [HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/august-payrolls-fed-focus/)
- 2026-08-31: Forbes reported that CME FedWatch put the chance of a September hike at 66%. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/digital-assets/2026/08/31/cme-fedwatch-provides-a-66-chance-fed-will-hike-rates-in-september/)
- 2026-08-28: At Jackson Hole, Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation is still too high and the Fed may need to raise rates "in the coming months," without committing to a date. AP said this raised the stakes for September and that the CPI report due just before the meeting could decide it. [ADN/AP](https://www.adn.com/nation-world/2026/08/28/fed-chair-warsh-signals-rate-hikes-may-be-needed-with-inflation-stubbornly-elevated/), [ClickOnDetroit/AP](https://www.clickondetroit.com/business/2026/08/29/warsh-raises-stakes-for-feds-next-meeting-and-other-takeaways-from-jackson-hole-conference/)
- 2026-08-07: After a weak July jobs report, hike odds fell and CME priced about a 60% chance of a September hold. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html)
- 2026-07-29: The FOMC held at 3.50%-3.75% on a 9-3 vote. Logan, Hammack and Kashkari dissented in favor of a 25 bp hike. Four regional Fed banks had asked for a higher discount rate. [BGov](https://news.bgov.com/banking-law/fed-holds-rates-three-officials-dissent-favoring-a-hike-2), [investinglive](https://investinglive.com/central-banks/four-regional-fed-banks-sought-discount-rate-hike-ahead-of-july-fomc-hold/)

## 4. Base rates
- July was the fifth meeting in a row with no change, which covers every 2026 meeting so far. [BGov](https://news.bgov.com/banking-law/fed-holds-rates-three-officials-dissent-favoring-a-hike-2)
- Generally, the Fed rarely moves against what markets have priced right before a meeting, and three or more dissents usually mean policy is about to shift. A hike would be the first since 2023.
- The 2026 Reuters polls have consistently expected holds: June 23-25, 78 of 102 economists expected no change all year; Aug 12-17, 94 of 104 expected a September hold. [Kitco Jun](https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-06-26/fed-hold-rates-year-economists-say-defying-market-bets-hikes-reuters), [Kitco Aug](https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-08-17/fed-hold-interest-rates-year-economists-say-sticking-their-view)

## 5. Other forecasts
- About 2026-09-10: one aggregator reported CME FedWatch at 0.0% cut, **37.6% no change** and 62.4% for a 25 bp hike. I couldn't confirm this directly. [growbeansprout](https://growbeansprout.com/tools/fedwatch)
- About 2026-09-08 to 09-10, exact date unclear: a Polymarket dashboard showed a 25 bp hike at 62% and **no change at 39%**. Another source said one comparison had CME futures at 64% for a hike and Polymarket/Kalshi at 56-58%. [cryptonews](https://cryptonews.com/news/polymarket-fed-rates-september-hike/), [macroodds](https://macroodds.com/blog/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026)
- 2026-09-04: Polymarket had a hike at 51.5% and Kalshi at 54%, so a hold was about 46-48%. [predictionmarketspicks](https://predictionmarketspicks.com/articles/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026-kalshi-polymarket-futures)
- Around Jackson Hole: Kalshi priced a hike at 48% and Polymarket at 49%. [Chase](https://www.chase.com/personal/investments/learning-and-insights/article/september-2026-rate-hike-now-expected-amid-energy-shocks)
- Economists lean more toward a hold than markets do. The Aug 12-17 Reuters poll had 90% expecting a hold. A later Reuters-cited poll, possibly from early September, had 65 of 93 (about 70%) expecting a hold, but I couldn't confirm its exact date. [Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-08-17/fed-hold-interest-rates-year-economists-say-sticking-their-view), [tech-insider](https://tech-insider.org/polymarket-fed-september-2026-rate-odds/)
- Overall, on Sept 10 markets put a hold at roughly 35-40%, while economist surveys still mostly expected one.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The **August CPI** report is due about Sept 11, after this question closes. Sources treat it as the deciding input: core CPI at 0.2% month on month was seen as consistent with a hold, and a hotter reading would favor a hike. [Admiral Markets](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/us-cpi-preview-september-2026-forecasts-and-the-core-cpi-outlook), [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/fed-rate-hike-odds-core-cpi-september-2026)
- PPI and retail sales for August should also come out the week of Sept 14.
- The Fed's pre-meeting blackout period means officials won't comment publicly until the decision.
- The FOMC statement and new Summary of Economic Projections come out Sept 16.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I found no announced change to the target range before the September 15-16 meeting, so nothing settles the question yet. As of September 10, futures and prediction markets put a 25 bp hike as the slight-to-moderate favourite over "no change." Fetching pages failed every time (the proxy refused the connection), so everything below comes from search-result summaries. Many results were dated after the cutoff, and I left those out.

## 1. Resolution source
- I could not load federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm or the FOMC calendar, so I can't report what those pages show.
- 2026-07-29: The FOMC held the target range at 3.50%-3.75%. That was the fifth hold in a row, so the September baseline upper bound is 3.75%. [FHLB Boston](https://www.fhlbboston.com/strategies-insights/july-29-2026-fomc-meeting-analysis/), [PCBB](https://www.pcbb.com/industry-insights/economy/2026-07-29-fomc-july-2026)
- The next meeting is scheduled for September 15-16, 2026, with the statement due September 16.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the outcome.
- The choice is between holding and hiking 25 bp. No source I found discussed a cut. Until about August 15 the market mostly expected a hold. It has shifted sharply toward a hike since then.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-07: Fortune reported that Wall Street was moving toward expecting a hike while the White House stepped up pressure on Chair Warsh. About 60% of futures bets were on a 25 bp hike to 3.75%-4.00%. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/09/07/wall-street-hike-expectations-kevin-warsh-fed-trump/)
- 2026-09-05: Trump pushed the Fed to cut rates ahead of the September decision. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/05/trump-warsh-fed-september-rate-hike.html)
- 2026-09-04: The August jobs report showed +162k payrolls against a 53k consensus, with unemployment at 4.1% and upward revisions to earlier months. Axios said this gives the Fed less reason to hold off on a hike. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-august-2026.html), [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-labor-fed-rates)
- Early September (exact date not confirmed): Governor Waller said he would be willing to hold if the August CPI, due September 11, shows inflation still cooling. If it comes in hot, he would consider a hike. Hike odds dropped from about 65% to roughly 50-50 after his comments. NY Fed President Williams also signalled he was open to holding. [PBS](https://pbs.org/newshour/economy/fed-governor-waller-muddies-outlook-on-possible-rate-hike-later-this-month), [Qatar Tribune](https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/252005/business/fed-rate-hike-still-in-play-as-waller-awaits-inflation-data)
- 2026-08-31: CNBC wrote that markets expect Warsh to back a September hike, but not everyone is convinced. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/31/markets-see-warsh-endorsing-a-rate-hike-in-september-not-everyone-is-convinced.html)
- 2026-08-28: In his Jackson Hole speech, Warsh said the Fed may have "more work to do" and that its focus should be on prices because inflation is above 2%. CNBC called September "a coin flip" afterwards. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)
- 2026-07-29: The hold vote was 9-3. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented in favour of a 25 bp hike. The statement cited high inflation linked to energy and supply shocks from the Middle East conflict, and gave no forward guidance. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/three-fed-members-dissent-for-rate-hike-amid-inflation-concerns), [XTB](https://www.xtb.com/sca-en/market-analysis/news-and-research/breaking-fed-keeps-rates-unchanged-amid-regional-dissents-and-warsh-s-pause)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-07-29: That was the fifth straight unchanged decision, so every 2026 meeting through July has been "no change." [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/three-fed-members-dissent-for-rate-hike-amid-inflation-concerns)
- Historically, the Fed rarely goes against market pricing that is strongly one-sided going into the blackout period. Here, though, pricing was close to even, roughly 50-65% for a hike. I did not find a systematic base rate for meetings priced like this.
- Three hawkish dissents in July point to a turn toward tightening. In past cycles, the Fed has often started hiking within one or two meetings after dissents like that.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-07: CME FedWatch had about 60% for a 25 bp hike and about 40% for a hold. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/09/07/wall-street-hike-expectations-kevin-warsh-fed-trump/)
- 2026-09-04: Polymarket had 51.5% and Kalshi 54% for a 25 bp hike, with "no change" around 47% on both. [MacroOdds](https://macroodds.com/blog/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026)
- 2026-09-02: The Kalshi hike contract was at 58 cents, up from 26 cents on August 15. [PredictionMarketsPicks](https://predictionmarketspicks.com/articles/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026-kalshi-polymarket-futures)
- Another snapshot showed Polymarket at 53% for a hike against 32% in futures, but its date is unclear. Separate Polymarket figures of 62% hike / 39% no change also appeared without a confirmed date. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/polymarket-prices-53-odds-of-fed-rate-hike-in-september-2026-vs-32-in-futures), [Cryptonews](https://cryptonews.com/news/polymarket-fed-rates-september-hike/)
- One September 2026 article said Polymarket and Kalshi traders were raising their hike odds before the CPI release. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/09/61643866/polymarket-and-kalshi-traders-boost-fed-rate-hike-odds-as-us-inflation-report-looms)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-11: The August CPI comes out after forecasts close. Waller called it the deciding factor, and analysts treat it as the swing data point. [Qatar Tribune](https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/252005/business/fed-rate-hike-still-in-play-as-waller-awaits-inflation-data)
- Around 2026-09-11/12: August PPI and retail sales are likely, but I did not confirm the dates.
- 2026-09-15/16: The FOMC meets, with the statement, Summary of Economic Projections and Warsh's press conference on September 16. Fed officials are in the blackout period, so they will not speak publicly before then.
- Pressure from Trump and the White House to cut is ongoing. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/05/trump-warsh-fed-september-rate-hike.html)
